transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Hello. Um... well, I suppose I'm just having a hard time turning off my thoughts. The worrying, I mean. 

Once it gets started, I just can't seem to stop it. Even when I tell myself I've already... you know, made the list, checked the dates, and done everything I reasonably can. It just doesn't turn off.
Do you notice any physical symptoms, like restlessness, muscle tension, or trouble sleeping, when you're feeling this way?

Well... I suppose I do get a bit wound up. Even just sitting in my own living room. I'll find myself... tapping my fingers during phone calls, or getting up to straighten something. Sitting quietly just makes me feel a little jumpy, I guess.
Do these worries tend to focus on specific things, like social situations, or do they jump around a lot between different topics?

I suppose they jump around... yes. My mind just sort of keeps roaming. 

I'll be thinking about the exhibition schedule, and then... well, then it's my daughter's travel plans. Or whether the house gutters need fixing. Just... everyday things. But then those small things start to feel as if they might... I don't know, unravel into something much bigger, I guess.
Do you find it very hard to control the worrying, even when you know it might not make sense or you’ve already taken care of the problem?

Um... yes, I suppose that's right. I try to just put it out of my mind once a task is finished, but... it doesn't always work. It just sort of stays with me. I'm not really sure how else to explain it.
Does this constant worrying affect your ability to function in your daily life, like at work, with family, or in social situations?

Well... I suppose I still manage most things. I still go to my book club, and I keep up with the garden. But... I don't know, I guess I've been a bit less prepared lately. And... I did step back from some of the exhibition planning. It just... it feels a bit harder to manage than it used to, I suppose.

Have you ever experienced sudden episodes where you feel intense fear or discomfort that comes on quickly and peaks within minutes, like your heart racing, feeling short of breath, or as if you're losing control?
No... no, I haven't had anything like that. Just the worrying, really. Nothing sudden.
Do you find yourself worrying even when things are going smoothly, or does it mostly happen when there's something specific that needs attention?

Well... I suppose it happens even when things are fine. My mind just... keeps roaming, I guess. I'll be thinking about the exhibition schedule, and then... well, my daughter's travel plans, or... wondering whether the gutters on the house need fixing. Just... small things, really. But they start to feel as if they could... I don't know, unravel into something much bigger. It just sort of... happens.
Do you ever feel the need to do certain things over and over again, like checking, counting, or following specific routines, even if you know they're not really necessary?
No, I... I don't think so. I don't really do anything like that. I just... worry, like I said.
Would you say that you feel anxious or worried about things on most days, even when there isn’t anything specific that needs your attention?
Well... yes, I suppose so. Most days, I think. Even when there isn't anything pressing. It's just... always there in the background.
Have you ever felt sudden physical symptoms like dizziness, sweating, or chest pain when you're not sure why they're happening?
No... I don't think so. I haven't really had anything like that happen. Just... what I mentioned before.
Have you ever felt driven to perform certain actions or rituals repeatedly, even if you didn’t want to, because you felt you had to?
No... I don't. I think you asked me something similar a minute ago, but... no. I don't have any rituals or anything like that.
Would you say that your anxiety or worry interferes with your ability to relax, even during times when you don't have much going on?

Yes, I suppose so. Even just... sitting in my own living room, I can feel a bit wound up. I'll find myself tapping my fingers if I'm on the phone, or... I just have to get up and straighten things around the room. Sitting completely quiet just... it makes me a little jumpy, I guess.
Would you say that you feel anxious or worried about a number of different things on most days, even when there isn't a clear reason for concern?

I suppose I do. It's just... my mind keeps roaming, I guess. I'll be thinking about... well, the exhibition schedule, or my daughter's travel plans. Or even just whether the house gutters need fixing. Just everyday things. But sometimes those small things start to feel as if they could... unravel into something much bigger. So... yes, I guess I do.
Would you say that your worrying makes it hard for you to carry out your usual activities, like work, spending time with family, or enjoying your hobbies, even if you still manage to do them?

I suppose... a little. I mean, I still keep up with the garden, and I still go to my book club. But... well, I guess I've been arriving a bit less prepared lately. And the exhibition planning... I've actually started turning down some parts of that. It just... it feels a bit harder to manage than it used to. So, yes, I guess it does.
Would you say that you feel anxious or worried on more days than not, and has this been going on for some time now?
Yes, I suppose I do. It's been... well, maybe about seven months now. Since shortly after... my friend passed away. I tried to just keep our projects moving, but... yes, it's been since around then.
